headline: Bitcoin held near $80,000 into Thursday in Asia after a short squeeze, while Binance says $2.85 billion tied to its record hack has been frozen or intercepted.

market.asOf: From the Why It Moved daily market report for Thu 5 Nov (posted early 5 Nov UTC; it gives no exact time for crypto prices and labels the changes as the day's move). CoinGecko, CoinMarketCap and the Alternative.me index could not be opened this run. For current prices, use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 34 (Fear) on the Crypto Fear & Greed Index, per the Why It Moved report for 5 Nov; the report does not name the index provider.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $80,000 after a short squeeze, while fund investors kept selling
stories.summary: Bitcoin had fallen as low as about $75,700 before jumping back above $80,000 as traders who had bet on further falls were forced to buy back. It was still near $80,000 early Thursday in Asia. US bitcoin funds kept losing money through Tuesday, so leveraged traders, not new fund buying, drove the bounce.
points: Bitcoin was about $80,464 (+3.4%) and ether about $2,423 (+5.9%) in the Why It Moved report for 5 Nov.
$915M of positions were liquidated in 24 hours, $555M of them bets on falling prices, per CoinGlass data cited by crypto.news.
US spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $398.6M on 2 Nov, per Live Bitcoin News, and $115.6M on 3 Nov, per SoSoValue data cited by Analytics Insight.
US ether ETFs lost $85.3M on 3 Nov, a seventh straight day of outflows, per Live Bitcoin News.
Strategy and Coinbase shares both rose about 6% on 4 Nov, per The Block.

stories.title: Binance says $2.85 billion tied to its hack is frozen or intercepted, but laundering goes on
stories.summary: Binance co-CEO Richard Teng says about $2.85 billion linked to the 29 October attack has been frozen or intercepted and customers will not bear the losses. Blockchain tracker Elliptic puts the total stolen at $6.43 billion, with more than $3 billion still in wallets tied to the theft and some of it being moved through THORChain.
points: About $2.85B has been frozen or intercepted and 98% of affected tokens have been replenished, Teng said, per TokenPost.
Elliptic puts the total stolen at $6.43B, with 44% frozen or seized and about $3.21B still in addresses tied to the theft.
Circle froze all 823M stolen USDC before any of it could be swapped, per Elliptic.
After THORChain resumed swaps, about 4,600 ETH was moved through it into bitcoin, per Elliptic.
Binance's net outflows reached $5.28B after the hack, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: After their sweep, House Democrats sketch a crypto bill with a bigger SEC role
stories.summary: House Democrats are discussing their own crypto market-structure bill for the next Congress, which would give the SEC more oversight and the CFTC a smaller role. The industry-backed CLARITY Act is now seen as unlikely to move, and Republicans call the Democratic idea a messaging bill.
points: The plan would build on Maxine Waters' 2025 investor-protection amendment to the CLARITY Act, per crypto.news.
It could add ethics rules restricting crypto dealings by the President and other federal officials, per crypto.news.
CLARITY failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 in September, per crypto.news.
TD Cowen says CLARITY is unlikely to advance over the next two years, per The Block.
